name: Daily Mail cryptic crossword, book 2 No 83

book.title: Daily Mail New Cryptic Crosswords, volume 2

clue.text: Confront rise that may improve appearance

blocks.note: to face something is to confront it
a lift is a rise or raising

explanation.surface: Someone squares up to a pay rise, or a hairline, hoping it will smarten their looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetic surgery tightening facial skin is done precisely to make someone look younger and better.

clue.text: Known for a short time in drama left unfinished

indicators.note: a work left unfinished is missing its ending, so the final letter goes
the brief period sits inside the shortened title of the play

blocks.note: the title of Goethe's and Marlowe's play about a man who sells his soul
a mo is a moment

explanation.surface: A play abandoned halfway had a brief spell of fame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drama' looks generic, but the setter wants one specific play by name; cutting its last letter and inserting MO gives FAMOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous people are widely recognised; 'known for' is the phrase used of celebrated things.

clue.text: Fire said to bring a fall

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word for fire is to be heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: to fire a gun is to shoot

explanation.surface: Opening fire, it is claimed, brings someone down.
explanation.definitionFit: A chute is a steep channel or waterfall, a drop down which water or objects fall.

clue.text: Gone for good after a time

blocks.note: first meaning: dead
second meaning: arriving after the appointed hour

explanation.surface: Someone has left for ever after a while.
explanation.definitionFit: The deceased are called 'the late', and anyone missing the appointed hour arrives behind schedule.

clue.text: Militant in fact a trouble-maker

indicators.note: making trouble stirs things into disorder, so the preceding letters get scrambled

blocks.note: the letters of these three words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A hardliner revealed to be a stirrer after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble-maker' reads as a noun describing the militant, but it is what makes the letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealot with extreme, uncompromising views is a militant in the noun sense.

clue.text: Support needed when there's delay

blocks.note: first meaning: to prop or bear the weight of
second meaning: a stoppage, as in traffic

explanation.surface: A plea for backing when things are running late.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb phrase and the noun share their letters; the hyphenated noun is the answer, the two-word verb is the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic stoppages are called hold-ups, while holding up a beam means bearing its weight from below.

clue.text: Giving not outstanding due

blocks.note: surface padding: a hint that whoever has not yet given what is required is still in debt
first meaning: not yet paid, as a debt still unsettled
second meaning: payable now

explanation.surface: A debtor not paying up what is owed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giving not' is a hint rather than wordplay: whoever has not yet given what they should is still in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Money yet to be paid is both outstanding and due, words used of an unsettled debt.

clue.text: Talk of dance party sure to be misinterpreted

indicators.note: a misinterpreted word is read wrongly, so its letters come out in another order

blocks.note: a disco is a dance party
the letters of sure rearranged

explanation.surface: Chatter at a dance about something certain that is bound to be misunderstood.
explanation.definitionFit: Discourse is formal spoken or written communication, i.e. conversation or speech on a subject.

clue.text: March is included to give delight

indicators.note: being included means being placed inside the other word

blocks.note: a march is a parade
taken as written

explanation.surface: A procession, once included, brings joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month, but it is the verb or noun for a procession.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is a state of perfect bliss or happiness, so it serves as a noun for delight.

clue.text: Getting more prepared for a ride

blocks.note: first meaning: increasing, as bills or pressure keep rising
second meaning: climbing onto a horse or bicycle before setting off

explanation.surface: Someone gets ever keener as they ready themselves for an outing.
explanation.definitionFit: Costs that keep increasing are said to be mounting, and a rider climbing into the saddle is mounting too.

clue.text: One making contact in the park is seriously deceived

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, spanning their boundaries
the eye is fooled into reading separate words where a single word lies concealed

blocks.note: the end of park, the whole of is and the start of seriously run together

explanation.surface: A couple canoodling on a park bench turns out to have been badly fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: A kisser is one person making contact with lips, and it is also slang for the mouth itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who kisses brings their lips into touch with another person, so they are literally making contact.

clue.text: Not everybody understands the fish is English

blocks.note: cod is a fish
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Few people get that this fish is English.
explanation.definitionFit: A cipher is a secret system of writing that only those with the key can read.

clue.text: Not new for a sailor to depart when sworn at

indicators.note: the sailor leaving means those letters are taken out of the longer word

blocks.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
being sworn at is being verbally insulted

explanation.surface: A seaman storms off after being cursed at, which is nothing new for him.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the AB off ABUSED to leave USED.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand goods are described as used, meaning they have already had an earlier owner.

clue.text: Powerful grip that may provide protection

blocks.note: powerful means strong
a grip is a hold

explanation.surface: A firm clasp that keeps someone safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortress or fortified place shelters its defenders, so it is somewhere offering safety from attack.

clue.text: Not favouring wine when some of the chill is missing

indicators.note: what is missing has gone, so those letters are removed from the wine

blocks.note: Chianti is an Italian red wine
the opening letters of chill

explanation.surface: Someone who dislikes wine that is served less than chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove CH, the start of chill, from CHIANTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti as a preposition or adjective means opposed to something, the reverse of being in favour.

clue.text: They go to some lengths in fear of emergency actions

blocks.note: panic is sudden fear

blocks.clueFragment: They go to some lengths in
blocks.note: rulers and tapes are measures, used to find lengths

explanation.surface: Frightened people will go to great lengths when a crisis strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go to some lengths' sounds like effort, but measures literally go to lengths: a measure is how long something is.
explanation.definitionFit: Hasty steps taken under pressure in a crisis are called panic measures, i.e. rushed responses to sudden danger.

clue.text: Gasp when a bird is seen as a comic character

blocks.note: to pant is to gasp for breath
taken as written
a loon is a diving bird, the North American name for a diver

explanation.surface: An audience gasps when a bird-like clown appears on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantaloon is the foolish old man of Italian commedia and English pantomime, a stock figure of fun.

clue.text: A lot of people can move away from French island

indicators.note: moving away from something leaves it behind, so those letters are taken off

blocks.note: mobile means able to move
île is French for island

explanation.surface: A crowd is able to leave an island off France.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop ILE from the end of MOBILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mob is a large, often disorderly crowd, so it is a great many people gathered together.

clue.text: Possessions as disposed of for collections

indicators.note: what is disposed of is got rid of, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: assets are things one owns
taken as written

explanation.surface: Belongings sold off to make up a set of items for collectors.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove AS from the front of ASSETS.
explanation.definitionFit: A set is a group of matching items kept together, such as a set of stamps or china.

clue.text: Investigation about rating starting to look likely

indicators.note: starting points to only the opening letter of the next word
the inquiry goes around the other pieces, enclosing them

blocks.note: a probe is an investigation
a rating is a non-officer sailor, the able seaman AB
first letter of look

explanation.surface: An inquiry into a credit score begins to seem promising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rating' suggests a score, but in the Royal Navy a rating is an ordinary sailor, so it gives the able seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Probable describes what will most likely happen, so it is a near synonym of likely.

clue.text: In which a fight becomes a moving experience

definitions.text: In which a fight becomes a moving experience

blocks.note: surface reading: an emotionally touching event

blocks.clueFragment: a fight becomes a moving experience
blocks.note: setter's reading: a conflict that literally moves along, the combatants on the go as they fight

explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' suggests emotion, but it means travelling: the fight keeps shifting ground, or drags on over time.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-continued fight, carried on while the parties keep moving, is the idiom for an ongoing dispute or skirmish.

clue.text: Show surprise as the doctor comes round

indicators.note: coming round means encircling, so the doctor's letters wrap the other word

blocks.note: a GP, general practitioner, is a family doctor
taken as written

explanation.surface: A patient is startled when the physician wakes from unconsciousness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comes round' suggests waking up, but it means the doctor surrounds AS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp intake of breath is the classic involuntary reaction of someone shocked or astonished.

clue.text: A weekend a number of people find amazing

blocks.note: taken as written
w/e is the usual abbreviation for weekend
some means an unspecified number

explanation.surface: Several friends think a couple of days off is wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inspiring wonder or great admiration is awesome, the informal intensifier for astonishing or terrific.

clue.text: Speaker otherwise reaching a high point

blocks.note: or means otherwise
taken as written
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A lecturer who instead attains a peak of eloquence.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a craggy hilltop in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An orator is a public speaker, especially one skilled at persuasive formal addresses.

clue.text: Waved the mark one took off

blocks.note: a brand is a mark burned or stamped on
I is the Roman numeral one
to shed is to take off, as clothing or skin

explanation.surface: Someone flaps a hand as a label or stain is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To brandish is to flourish a weapon or object threateningly, swinging it about in the air.

clue.text: Talk of dropping commercial cover

indicators.note: dropping means letting go of, so those letters are left out

blocks.note: an address is a formal talk
an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: A speech about leaving off the advertising cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove AD from the front of ADDRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress is to clothe, and clothing covers the body; also a dressing covers a wound.

clue.text: Move to cause a commotion

blocks.note: first meaning: to move slightly, as a sleeper does
second meaning: to ... things up, provoking trouble

explanation.surface: An instruction to get going and make a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeper begins to stir on waking, and a troublemaker likes to stir up unrest among other people.

clue.text: One seeking to support a view of the land?

definitions.text: One seeking to support a view

blocks.clueFragment: One seeking to support a view
blocks.note: first meaning: a pamphlet arguing a religious or political position
second meaning: an expanse of ground

explanation.surface: Someone propping up a scenic panorama of the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A view of the land' reads as scenery, but a view is an opinion and the land a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A pamphlet promoting an opinion is a tract, and an area of country is also a tract.

clue.text: Something of a lesser evil when dry

indicators.note: something of means only a part, here a run of letters within the words

blocks.note: the tail of lesser and the first letter of evil

explanation.surface: Drought counts as the smaller of two misfortunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sere is a literary adjective for withered or parched, describing vegetation that has dried out.

clue.text: One who can trumpet on the phone?

definitions.note: the slang appears in the phrase 'on the blower'

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who blows an instrument
second meaning: British slang for a telephone

explanation.surface: A braggart, or brass player, who is talking on the telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the blower' is old British slang for being on the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone sounding a trumpet must blow into it, and Britons have long called their telephone by this slang name.

clue.text: Take in nothing about core of trouble anticipated

indicators.note: the abstinence word goes around the other letters, surrounding them
something in trouble is in disorder, so its letters are thrown about

blocks.note: to fast is to eat nothing at all
the four letters of core rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who eats nothing foresaw the heart of the trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take in' looks like deceive or understand, but taking in nothing means going without food. 'Core' is the fodder, not a request for middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To forecast is to predict, so something forecast has been foreseen or expected in advance.

clue.text: Serious article lacking a name

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so that letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: earnest means serious, sincere
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A grave newspaper piece omitting a person's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Take A out of EARNEST; a wink at Wilde's play The Importance of Being Earnest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a man's given name, so it is an example of a name.

clue.text: One may betray something wrong otherwise

blocks.note: a defect is a fault
or means otherwise, as in 'hurry or you'll be late'

explanation.surface: A warning that a fault could give someone away.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abandons their country or side for the enemy is a traitor who betrays former allies.
